verses.1: In those days, there was no king in Israel. There was a man who lived in the wilderness of Ephraim. He married a woman from the household of Leah.
verses.2: And Filagsho covered him with a cloak. Then she went away from him to her father’s house, to the house of Lehem Yehuda. There she stayed for four days.
verses.3: And she got up and went after him to talk to her heart out, in order to comfort her. She brought the boy with her, along with some woolen clothes. Then she brought him back to her father’s house. When her father saw him, he was very happy to see him again.
verses.4: And through him, our inheritance was strengthened. Our father, the young man, stayed there for three days. They ate, drank, and slept there.
verses.5: And on the fourth day, they got up in the morning. They decided to go out. They said to their young man, “My father, go with your bride. Bring some bread for her. Then you can leave.”
verses.6: And they sat down and ate together. Then they slept. And the young woman said to the man, “Please, may your heart be filled with peace.”
verses.7: And the man got up to go. He prepared his inheritance for himself, then sat down and remained there.
verses.8: And they rested in the evening, on the fifth day before they had to leave. He said, “Father, please go with me.” Then he became very tired until the end of the day. And they ate together.
verses.9: And the man got up to go. He split his clothes and left with his young son. He said to him, “My son, today you must rest for the day. Please rest here today. May your heart be at peace tomorrow when you start your journey. Then you can go to your own home.”
verses.10: And that man did not go to Loun. He got up and went on his way. He arrived at Jerusalem. With him were his servants and slaves, along with his family.
verses.11: They were with Yevus. Today, he came down from high places. The boy said to his father, “Please go and try to get us out of this city of Yevus. Let’s get away from here.”
verses.12: And Adonai said to him, “Do not enter into a foreign city that has not been built by Israel. We have already passed through its territory.”
verses.13: And he said to the young man, “Go to one of those places and stand there. Then you can bring me the soil or the earth.”
verses.14: And they went away. Then the sun shone upon them, right beside the golden altar.
verses.15: They refused to go there and enter the forest. They came instead and sat down in a quiet place in the city. No one was there to help them get into the forest.
verses.16: And behold, an old man came out from his work in the field at noon. The man rushed from the wilderness, and he lived in the wilderness. And the people of that place were sons of the right hand.
verses.17: He raised his eyes and saw the old man walking in the center of the city. The old man said, “Go away from here.”
verses.18: And he said to him, “Let us pass from the house of Leah in Judah until we reach the Mount of Efrathi. Then I will go on to the house of Leah in Judah. I will go there, and no one will stop me.”
verses.19: And also, there is bread and wine for our ancestors. And also, there is bread and wine for me and for your true love. And for the young man with your servants, nothing can be hidden from them.
verses.20: And the old man said, “May peace be with you. But all your possessions are still in my possession. Do not worry about them.”
verses.21: And he brought him into his house. Then he washed his feet, and they ate and drank.
verses.22: Many people were pleased with this. Then, the people of the city, the sons of Bliyal, rushed into the house and knocked on the door. They said to the old man who owned the house, “Let’s go out and see who it is who has come to your house.”
verses.23: And the man who owned the house went out to them and said, “My brothers, please do not harm anyone because of this man who has come here. Do not do this horrible thing.”
verses.24: Look, my daughter! Please find them and bring them back. Do what is right in your eyes for them. But do not do anything that would harm this man.
verses.25: And they refused to listen to him. So the man became more determined in his efforts. He went out to them, and they knew who he was. They abused him all night long until morning. Then they sent her away as slaves.
verses.26: And the woman went to meet him in the morning. She entered the man’s house, where her master was staying until evening.
verses.27: In the morning, Adonai stood up. He opened the doors of the house, and he went out to go his way. And there was a woman lying at the entrance of the house, with her hands on the doorposts.
verses.28: And he said to her, “Get up, let’s go. There is no one else here.” Then he took her by the hand and she got up. The man also got up and went to his place.
verses.29: And she went into her house, took the food, and strengthened herself with it. Then she had twelve surgeries performed on her body. After that, she was sent out across all the borders of Israel.
verses.30: And all those who saw it said, “It will never be like this again.” From the day when the children of Israel left Egypt until today, they have been discussing and talking about it.
